newsitem.title: USA: Canandaigua seeks to calm investor worries.
newsitem.headline: Canandaigua seeks to calm investor worries.

text.p: Canandaigua Wine Co Inc sought to calm jittery investors in a conference call Friday morning, saying "problems are being addressed and corrected by management".

Late Thursday, the company cut profit estimates for the fiscal year ending February 28, 1997 sharply, saying its wine division performed poorly and its estimate of a last-in, first-out (LIFO) adjustment grew due to higher costs.
The stock dropped about 20 percent at the opening, off 4-1/4 to 17-3/4, touching a new year low of 17-1/2.
Canandaigua said internal operating inefficiencies, high grape prices, and a general slowing of growth in the wine industry also hurt its performance.

To remedy the internal inefficiencies, the company said: "We are implementing new management information systems to better measure and control efficiencies, new leadership at our Mission Bell facilty, (including a new plant manager) and new financial management within the wine division ... And in the longer term, we'refocusing on work processing systems and organizaiton. We believe our efforts will ... drive our wine business forward ... and lead to improved results."

But Canandaigua declined to discuss specifics. "We are preparing to announce our changes ... to our internal organization shortly and until then, we are not in a position to discuss the details with the financial community," it said.
The company said it expects some one-time costs from the changes but not any significant restructuring charge.

High prices in the grape market also added to the poor performance, Canandaigua said. But it said "If we had not had the external influence of grape price increases, we would have still had significant internal disruption with regard to operating inefficiencies," it said.

"As we began to crush grapes, we found pricing was higher," it said. Although it believes grape prices may drop, in line with historical industry cycles, "It is difficult to predict what prices will be during harvest and next year."

Canandaigua also said industry wide price increases hurt growth trends. It also said white zinfandel sales, which had growing about 6 pct, reversed to a loss of two percent in July, citing Neilson's ratings.
The company stressed the performance at its Barton beer and spirits division was better than expected.
Canandaigua Wine is based in Canandaigua, N.Y..
